<summary><h2> What Can I Do with Hyperswitch?</h2></summary>

Hyperswitch offers a modular, open-source payments infrastructure designed for flexibility and control. Apart from our Payment Suite offering, this solution allows businesses to pick and integrate only the modules they need on top of their existing payment stack — without unnecessary complexity or vendor lock-in.

Each module is independent and purpose-built to optimize different aspects of payment processing.

<h3> Learn More About The Payment Modules </h3>
<details>

- **Cost Observability**  
  Advanced observability tools to audit, monitor, and optimize your payment costs. Detect hidden fees, downgrades, and penalties with self-serve dashboards and actionable insights.  
  _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/ai-powered-cost-observability)_

- **Revenue Recovery**  
  Combat passive churn with intelligent retry strategies tuned by card bin, region, method, and more. Offers fine-grained control over retry algorithms, penalty budgets, and recovery transparency.  
  _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/revenue-recovery)_

- **Vault**  
  A PCI-compliant vault service to store cards, tokens, wallets, and bank credentials. Provides a unified, secure, and reusable store of customer-linked payment methods.  
  _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/vault)_

- **Intelligent Routing**  
  Route each transaction to the PSP with the highest predicted auth rate. Reduce retries, avoid downtime, and minimize latency while maximizing first attempt success.  
  _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/intelligent-routing)_

- **Reconciliation**  
  Automate 2-way and 3-way reconciliation with backdated support, staggered scheduling, and customizable outputs. Reduces manual ops effort and increases audit confidence.  
  _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/reconciliation)_

- **Alternate Payment Methods**  
  Drop-in widgets for PayPal, Apple Pay, Google Pay, Samsung Pay, Pay by Bank, and BNPL providers like Klarna. Maximizes conversions with seamless one-click checkout.  
  _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/enable-alternate-payment-method-widgets)_

</details>

## Quickstart 

<h3> Local Setup via Docker </h3>

```bash
# One-click local setup

git clone --depth 1 --branch latest https://github.com/juspay/hyperswitch

cd hyperswitch

scripts/setup.sh
```
<details>
  <summary><strong>This script: </strong></summary>

  - Detects Docker/Podman  
  - Offers multiple deployment profiles:
    - **Standard**: App server + Control Center  
    - **Full**: Includes monitoring + schedulers  
    - **Minimal**: Standalone App server  
  - Provides access links when done

  If you need further help, check out our [video tutorial](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/hyperswitch-open-source/overview/unified-local-setup-using-docker).  

  👉 After setup, [configure a connector](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/hyperswitch-open-source/account-setup/using-hyperswitch-control-center#add-a-payment-processor) and [test a payment](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/hyperswitch-open-source/account-setup/test-a-payment).
</details>


<h3>Hosted Sandbox (No Setup Required)</h3>

Hyperswitch offers a fully hosted sandbox environment that requires no setup. You can explore the Control Center, configure payment connectors, and test payments directly from the UI.

  - Access the full Control Center  
  - Configure payment connectors  
  - View logs, routing rules, and retry strategies  
  - Try payments directly from the UI  
</details>

## Why Hyperswitch?

Hyperswitch is a commercial open-source payments stack purpose-built for scale, flexibility, and developer experience. Designed with a modular architecture, Hyperswitch lets you pick only the components you need—whether it’s routing, retries, vaulting, or observability—without vendor lock-in or bloated integrations.

Built in Rust for performance and reliability, Hyperswitch supports global payment methods (cards, wallets, BNPL, UPI, Pay by Bank), exposes smart routing and retry logic, and provides a visual workflow builder in the Control Center. Whether you're integrating a full payment suite or augmenting an existing stack with a single module, Hyperswitch meets you where you are.

<strong>“Linux for Payments”</strong> — Hyperswitch is a well-architected reference for teams who want to own their payments stack.

We believe in:

- <strong> Embracing Payment Diversity:</strong> Innovation comes from enabling choice—across payment methods, processors, and flows.

- <strong> Open Source by Default:</strong> Transparency drives trust and builds better, reusable software.

- <strong> Community-Driven Development:</strong> Our roadmap is shaped by real-world use cases and contributors. 

- <strong> Systems-Level Engineering:</strong> We hold ourselves to a high bar for reliability, security, and performance.

- <strong> Maximizing Value Creation:</strong> For developers, customers, and partners alike.

- <strong> Community-Driven, Enterprise-Tested:</strong> Hyperswitch is built in the open with real-world feedback from developers and contributors, and maintained by Juspay, the team powering payment infrastructure for 400+ leading enterprises worldwide.

## Contributing

We welcome contributors from around the world to help build Hyperswitch. Whether you're fixing bugs, improving documentation, or adding new features, your help is appreciated.

Please read our [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/juspay/hyperswitch/blob/main/docs/CONTRIBUTING.md) to get started.

Join the conversation on [Slack](https://inviter.co/hyperswitch-slack) or explore open issues on [GitHub](https://github.com/juspay/hyperswitch/issues).

449: impl TryFrom<&AirwallexRouterData<&types::PaymentsAuthorizeRouterData>>
450:     for AirwallexPaymentsRequest
451: {
452:     type Error = error_stack::Report<errors::ConnectorError>;
453:     fn try_from(
454:         item: &AirwallexRouterData<&types::PaymentsAuthorizeRouterData>,
455:     ) -> Result<Self, Self::Error> {
456:         let mut payment_method_options = None;
457:         let request = &item.router_data.request;
458:         let payment_method = match request.payment_method_data.clone() {
459:             PaymentMethodData::Card(ccard) => {
460:                 payment_method_options =
461:                     Some(AirwallexPaymentOptions::Card(AirwallexCardPaymentOptions {
462:                         auto_capture: matches!(
463:                             request.capture_method,
464:                             Some(enums::CaptureMethod::Automatic)
465:                                 | Some(enums::CaptureMethod::SequentialAutomatic)
466:                                 | None
467:                         ),
468:                     }));
469:                 Ok(AirwallexPaymentMethod::Card(AirwallexCard {
470:                     card: AirwallexCardDetails {
471:                         number: ccard.card_number.clone(),
472:                         expiry_month: ccard.card_exp_month.clone(),
473:                         expiry_year: ccard.get_expiry_year_4_digit(),
474:                         cvc: ccard.card_cvc,
475:                     },
476:                     payment_method_type: AirwallexPaymentType::Card,
477:                 }))
478:             }
479:             PaymentMethodData::Wallet(ref wallet_data) => get_wallet_details(wallet_data, item),
480:             PaymentMethodData::PayLater(ref paylater_data) => {
481:                 let paylater_options = AirwallexPayLaterPaymentOptions {
482:                     auto_capture: item.router_data.request.is_auto_capture()?,
483:                 };
484: 
485:                 payment_method_options = match paylater_data {
486:                     PayLaterData::KlarnaRedirect { .. } => {
487:                         Some(AirwallexPaymentOptions::Klarna(paylater_options))
488:                     }
489:                     PayLaterData::AtomeRedirect { .. } => {
490:                         Some(AirwallexPaymentOptions::Atome(paylater_options))
491:                     }
492:                     _ => None,
493:                 };
494: 
495:                 get_paylater_details(paylater_data, item)
496:             }
497:             PaymentMethodData::BankTransfer(ref banktransfer_data) => {
498:                 get_banktransfer_details(banktransfer_data, item)
499:             }
500:             PaymentMethodData::BankRedirect(ref bankredirect_data) => {
501:                 get_bankredirect_details(bankredirect_data, item)
502:             }
503:             PaymentMethodData::BankDebit(_)
504:             | PaymentMethodData::CardRedirect(_)
505:             | PaymentMethodData::Crypto(_)
506:             | PaymentMethodData::MandatePayment
507:             | PaymentMethodData::Reward
508:             | PaymentMethodData::RealTimePayment(_)
509:             | PaymentMethodData::MobilePayment(_)
510:             | PaymentMethodData::Upi(_)
511:             | PaymentMethodData::Voucher(_)
512:             | PaymentMethodData::GiftCard(_)
513:             | PaymentMethodData::OpenBanking(_)
514:             | PaymentMethodData::CardToken(_)
515:             | PaymentMethodData::NetworkToken(_)
516:             | PaymentMethodData::CardDetailsForNetworkTransactionId(_) => {
517:                 Err(errors::ConnectorError::NotImplemented(
518:                     utils::get_unimplemented_payment_method_error_message("airwallex"),
519:                 ))
520:             }
521:         }?;
522:         let device_data = get_device_data(item.router_data)?;
523: 
524:         let return_url = match &request.payment_method_data {
525:             PaymentMethodData::Wallet(wallet_data) => match wallet_data {
526:                 WalletData::PaypalRedirect(_paypal_details) => {
527:                     item.router_data.request.router_return_url.clone()
528:                 }
529:                 WalletData::Skrill(_) => item.router_data.request.router_return_url.clone(),
530:                 _ => request.complete_authorize_url.clone(),
531:             },
532:             PaymentMethodData::BankRedirect(_bankredirect_data) => {
533:                 item.router_data.request.router_return_url.clone()
534:             }
535:             PaymentMethodData::PayLater(_paylater_data) => {
536:                 item.router_data.request.router_return_url.clone()
537:             }
538:             _ => request.complete_authorize_url.clone(),
539:         };
540: 
541:         Ok(Self {
542:             request_id: Uuid::new_v4().to_string(),
543:             payment_method,
544:             payment_method_options,
545:             return_url,
546:             device_data,
547:         })
548:     }
549: }

551: fn get_device_data(
552:     item: &types::PaymentsAuthorizeRouterData,
553: ) -> Result<DeviceData, error_stack::Report<errors::ConnectorError>> {
554:     let info = item.request.get_browser_info()?;
555:     let browser = Browser {
556:         java_enabled: info.get_java_enabled()?,
557:         javascript_enabled: info.get_java_script_enabled()?,
558:         user_agent: info.get_user_agent()?,
559:     };
560:     let mobile = {
561:         let device_model = info.get_device_model().ok();
562:         let os_type = info.get_os_type().ok();
563:         let os_version = info.get_os_version().ok();
564: 
565:         if device_model.is_some() || os_type.is_some() || os_version.is_some() {
566:             Some(Mobile {
567:                 device_model,
568:                 os_type,
569:                 os_version,
570:             })
571:         } else {
572:             None
573:         }
574:     };
575:     Ok(DeviceData {
576:         accept_header: info.get_accept_header()?,
577:         browser,
578:         ip_address: info.get_ip_address()?,
579:         mobile,
580:         screen_color_depth: info.get_color_depth()?,
581:         screen_height: info.get_screen_height()?,
582:         screen_width: info.get_screen_width()?,
583:         timezone: info.get_time_zone()?.to_string(),
584:         language: info.get_language()?,
585:     })
586: }

612:                         country_code: item.router_data.get_billing_country().map_err(|_| {

626:     let not_implemented = Err(errors::ConnectorError::NotImplemented(

737:     let wallet_details: AirwallexPaymentMethod = match wallet_data {
738:         WalletData::GooglePay(gpay_details) => {
739:             let token = gpay_details
740:                 .tokenization_data
741:                 .get_encrypted_google_pay_token()
742:                 .attach_printable("Failed to get gpay wallet token")
743:                 .map_err(|_| errors::ConnectorError::MissingRequiredField {
744:                     field_name: "gpay wallet_token",

746:             AirwallexPaymentMethod::Wallets(AirwallexWalletData::GooglePay(GooglePayData {

748:                     encrypted_payment_token: Secret::new(token.clone()),
749:                     payment_data_type: GpayPaymentDataType::EncryptedPaymentToken,
750:                 },
751:                 payment_method_type: AirwallexPaymentType::Googlepay,
752:             }))
753:         }
754:         WalletData::PaypalRedirect(_paypal_details) => {
755:             AirwallexPaymentMethod::Wallets(AirwallexWalletData::Paypal(PaypalData {
756:                 paypal: PaypalDetails {
757:                     shopper_name: item
758:                         .router_data
759:                         .request
760:                         .customer_name
761:                         .as_ref()
762:                         .cloned()
763:                         .or_else(|| item.router_data.get_billing_full_name().ok())
764:                         .ok_or(errors::ConnectorError::MissingRequiredField {
765:                             field_name: "shopper_name",
766:                         })?,

768:                         errors::ConnectorError::MissingRequiredField {

770:                         }
771:                     })?,
772:                 },
773:                 payment_method_type: AirwallexPaymentType::Paypal,

778:                 skrill: SkrillDetails {
779:                     shopper_name: item
780:                         .router_data
781:                         .request
782:                         .customer_name
783:                         .as_ref()
784:                         .cloned()
785:                         .or_else(|| item.router_data.get_billing_full_name().ok())
786:                         .ok_or(errors::ConnectorError::MissingRequiredField {

967: fn get_payment_status(
968:     status: &AirwallexPaymentStatus,
969:     next_action: &Option<AirwallexNextAction>,
970: ) -> enums::AttemptStatus {
971:     match status.clone() {
972:         AirwallexPaymentStatus::Succeeded => enums::AttemptStatus::Charged,
973:         AirwallexPaymentStatus::Failed => enums::AttemptStatus::Failure,
974:         AirwallexPaymentStatus::Pending => enums::AttemptStatus::Pending,
975:         AirwallexPaymentStatus::RequiresPaymentMethod => enums::AttemptStatus::PaymentMethodAwaited,
976:         AirwallexPaymentStatus::RequiresCustomerAction => next_action.as_ref().map_or(
977:             enums::AttemptStatus::AuthenticationPending,
978:             |next_action| match next_action {
979:                 AirwallexNextAction::Payments(payments_next_action) => {
980:                     match payments_next_action.stage {
981:                         AirwallexNextActionStage::WaitingDeviceDataCollection => {
982:                             enums::AttemptStatus::DeviceDataCollectionPending
983:                         }
984:                         AirwallexNextActionStage::WaitingUserInfoInput => {
985:                             enums::AttemptStatus::AuthenticationPending
986:                         }
987:                     }
988:                 }
989:                 AirwallexNextAction::Redirect(_) => enums::AttemptStatus::AuthenticationPending,
990:             },
991:         ),
992:         AirwallexPaymentStatus::RequiresCapture => enums::AttemptStatus::Authorized,
993:         AirwallexPaymentStatus::Cancelled => enums::AttemptStatus::Voided,
994:     }
995: }

1116:     ) -> Result<Self, Self::Error> {

1118:             response,
1119:             data,
1120:             http_code,
1121:         } = item;
1122: 
1123:         match response {
1124:             AirwallexAuthorizeResponse::AirwallexPaymentsResponse(res) => {
1125:                 Self::try_from(ResponseRouterData::<
1126:                     F,
1127:                     AirwallexPaymentsResponse,

1130:                 > {

1136:             AirwallexAuthorizeResponse::AirwallexRedirectResponse(res) => {
1137:                 Self::try_from(ResponseRouterData::<
1138:                     F,
1139:                     AirwallexRedirectResponse,
1140:                     T,
1141:                     PaymentsResponseData,
1142:                 > {

1152: impl<F, T> TryFrom<ResponseRouterData<F, AirwallexPaymentsResponse, T, PaymentsResponseData>>
1153:     for RouterData<F, T, PaymentsResponseData>
1154: {
1155:     type Error = error_stack::Report<errors::ConnectorError>;
1156:     fn try_from(
1157:         item: ResponseRouterData<F, AirwallexPaymentsResponse, T, PaymentsResponseData>,
1158:     ) -> Result<Self, Self::Error> {
1159:         let (status, redirection_data) = item.response.next_action.clone().map_or(
1160:             // If no next action is there, map the status and set redirection form as None
1161:             (
1162:                 get_payment_status(
1163:                     &item.response.status,
1164:                     &item
1165:                         .response
1166:                         .next_action
1167:                         .clone()
1168:                         .map(AirwallexNextAction::Payments)
1169:                         .clone(),
1170:                 ),
1171:                 None,
1172:             ),
1173:             |response_url_data| {
1174:                 // If the connector sends a customer action response that is already under
1175:                 // process from our end it can cause an infinite loop to break this this check
1176:                 // is added and fail the payment
1177:                 if matches!(
1178:                     (
1179:                         response_url_data.stage.clone(),
1180:                         item.data.status,
1181:                         item.response.status.clone(),
1182:                     ),
1183:                     // If the connector sends waiting for DDC and our status is already DDC Pending
1184:                     // that means we initiated the call to collect the data and now we expect a different response
1185:                     (
1186:                             AirwallexNextActionStage::WaitingDeviceDataCollection,
1187:                             enums::AttemptStatus::DeviceDataCollectionPending,
1188:                             _
1189:                         )
1190:                         // If the connector sends waiting for Customer Action and our status is already Authenticaition Pending
1191:                         // that means we initiated the call to authenticate and now we do not expect a requires_customer action
1192:                         // it will start a loop
1193:                         | (
1194:                             _,
1195:                             enums::AttemptStatus::AuthenticationPending,
1196:                             AirwallexPaymentStatus::RequiresCustomerAction,
1197:                         )
1198:                 ) {
1199:                     // Fail the payment for above conditions
1200:                     (enums::AttemptStatus::AuthenticationFailed, None)
1201:                 } else {
1202:                     (
1203:                         //Build the redirect form and update the payment status
1204:                         get_payment_status(
1205:                             &item.response.status,
1206:                             &item
1207:                                 .response
1208:                                 .next_action
1209:                                 .map(AirwallexNextAction::Payments)
1210:                                 .clone(),
1211:                         ),
1212:                         get_redirection_form(response_url_data),
1213:                     )
1214:                 }
1215:             },
1216:         );
1217: 
1218:         Ok(Self {
1219:             status,
1220:             reference_id: Some(item.response.id.clone()),
1221:             response: Ok(PaymentsResponseData::TransactionResponse {
1222:                 resource_id: ResponseId::ConnectorTransactionId(item.response.id.clone()),
1223:                 redirection_data: Box::new(redirection_data),
1224:                 mandate_reference: Box::new(None),
1225:                 connector_metadata: None,
1226:                 network_txn_id: None,
1227:                 connector_response_reference_id: Some(item.response.id),
1228:                 incremental_authorization_allowed: None,
1229:                 charges: None,
1230:             }),
1231:             ..item.data
1232:         })
1233:     }
1234: }

pub async fn call_connector_service_prerequisites_for_external_vault_proxy<
    F,
    RouterDReq,
    ApiRequest,
    D,
>(
    state: &SessionState,
    req_state: ReqState,
    merchant_context: &domain::MerchantContext,
    connector: api::ConnectorData,
    operation: &BoxedOperation<'_, F, ApiRequest, D>,
    payment_data: &mut D,
    customer: &Option<domain::Customer>,
    call_connector_action: CallConnectorAction,
    schedule_time: Option<time::PrimitiveDateTime>,
    header_payload: HeaderPayload,
    frm_suggestion: Option<storage_enums::FrmSuggestion>,
    business_profile: &domain::Profile,
    is_retry_payment: bool,
    should_retry_with_pan: bool,
    all_keys_required: Option<bool>,
) -> RouterResult<(
    domain::MerchantConnectorAccountTypeDetails,
    domain::MerchantConnectorAccountTypeDetails,
    Option<storage::CustomerUpdate>,
    RouterData<F, RouterDReq, router_types::PaymentsResponseData>,
)>
where
    F: Send + Clone + Sync,
    RouterDReq: Send + Sync,

    // To create connector flow specific interface data
    D: OperationSessionGetters<F> + OperationSessionSetters<F> + Send + Sync + Clone,
    D: ConstructFlowSpecificData<F, RouterDReq, router_types::PaymentsResponseData>,
    RouterData<F, RouterDReq, router_types::PaymentsResponseData>: Feature<F, RouterDReq> + Send,
    // To construct connector flow specific api
    dyn api::Connector:
        services::api::ConnectorIntegration<F, RouterDReq, router_types::PaymentsResponseData>,
{
    // get merchant connector account related to external vault
    let external_vault_source: id_type::MerchantConnectorAccountId = business_profile
        .external_vault_connector_details
        .clone()
        .map(|connector_details| connector_details.vault_connector_id.clone())
        .ok_or(errors::ApiErrorResponse::InternalServerError)
        .attach_printable("mca_id not present for external vault")?;

    let external_vault_merchant_connector_account_type_details =
        domain::MerchantConnectorAccountTypeDetails::MerchantConnectorAccount(Box::new(
            helpers::get_merchant_connector_account_v2(
                state,
                merchant_context.get_merchant_key_store(),
                Some(&external_vault_source),
            )
            .await?,
        ));

    let (
        merchant_connector_account_type_details,
        updated_customer,
        router_data,
        _tokenization_action,
    ) = call_connector_service_prerequisites(
        state,
        req_state,
        merchant_context,
        connector,
        operation,
        payment_data,
        customer,
        call_connector_action,
        schedule_time,
        header_payload,
        frm_suggestion,
        business_profile,
        is_retry_payment,
        should_retry_with_pan,
        all_keys_required,
    )
    .await?;
    Ok((
        merchant_connector_account_type_details,
        external_vault_merchant_connector_account_type_details,
        updated_customer,
        router_data,
    ))
}

#[cfg(feature = "v2")]
#[instrument(skip_all)]
pub async fn internal_call_connector_service_prerequisites<F, RouterDReq, ApiRequest, D>(
    state: &SessionState,
    merchant_context: &domain::MerchantContext,
    connector: api::ConnectorData,
    operation: &BoxedOperation<'_, F, ApiRequest, D>,
    payment_data: &mut D,
    business_profile: &domain::Profile,
) -> RouterResult<(
    domain::MerchantConnectorAccountTypeDetails,
    RouterData<F, RouterDReq, router_types::PaymentsResponseData>,
)>
where
    F: Send + Clone + Sync,
    RouterDReq: Send + Sync,

    // To create connector flow specific interface data
    D: OperationSessionGetters<F> + OperationSessionSetters<F> + Send + Sync + Clone,
    D: ConstructFlowSpecificData<F, RouterDReq, router_types::PaymentsResponseData>,
    RouterData<F, RouterDReq, router_types::PaymentsResponseData>: Feature<F, RouterDReq> + Send,
    // To construct connector flow specific api
    dyn api::Connector:
        services::api::ConnectorIntegration<F, RouterDReq, router_types::PaymentsResponseData>,
{
    let merchant_connector_details =
        payment_data
            .get_merchant_connector_details()
            .ok_or_else(|| {
                error_stack::report!(errors::ApiErrorResponse::InternalServerError)
                    .attach_printable("Merchant connector details not found in payment data")
            })?;
    let merchant_connector_account =
        domain::MerchantConnectorAccountTypeDetails::MerchantConnectorDetails(
            merchant_connector_details,
        );

    operation
        .to_domain()?
        .populate_payment_data(
            state,
            payment_data,
            merchant_context,
            business_profile,
            &connector,
        )
        .await?;

    let router_data = payment_data
        .construct_router_data(
            state,
            connector.connector.id(),
            merchant_context,
            &None,
            &merchant_connector_account,
            None,
            None,
        )
        .await?;

    Ok((merchant_connector_account, router_data))
}

 Hyperswitch offers a modular, open-source payments infrastructure designed for flexibility and control. Apart from our Payment Suite offering, this solution allows businesses to pick and integrate only the modules they need on top of their existing payment stack — without unnecessary complexity or vendor lock-in. Each module is independent and purpose-built to optimize different aspects of payment processing.

Learn More About The Payment Modules

- **Cost Observability** Advanced observability tools to audit, monitor, and optimize your payment costs. Detect hidden fees, downgrades, and penalties with self-serve dashboards and actionable insights. _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/ai-powered-cost-observability)_ - **Revenue Recovery** Combat passive churn with intelligent retry strategies tuned by card bin, region, method, and more. Offers fine-grained control over retry algorithms, penalty budgets, and recovery transparency. _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/revenue-recovery)_ - **Vault** A PCI-compliant vault service to store cards, tokens, wallets, and bank credentials. Provides a unified, secure, and reusable store of customer-linked payment methods. _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/vault)_ - **Intelligent Routing** Route each transaction to the PSP with the highest predicted auth rate. Reduce retries, avoid downtime, and minimize latency while maximizing first attempt success. _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/intelligent-routing)_ - **Reconciliation** Automate 2-way and 3-way reconciliation with backdated support, staggered scheduling, and customizable outputs. Reduces manual ops effort and increases audit confidence. _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/reconciliation)_ - **Alternate Payment Methods** Drop-in widgets for PayPal, Apple Pay, Google Pay, Samsung Pay, Pay by Bank, and BNPL providers like Klarna. Maximizes conversions with seamless one-click checkout. _[Read more](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/about-hyperswitch/payments-modules/enable-alternate-payment-method-widgets)_
## Quickstart

Local Setup via Docker

```bash # One-click local setup git clone --depth 1 --branch latest https://github.com/juspay/hyperswitch cd hyperswitch scripts/setup.sh ```
This script: - Detects Docker/Podman - Offers multiple deployment profiles: - **Standard**: App server + Control Center - **Full**: Includes monitoring + schedulers - **Minimal**: Standalone App server - Provides access links when done If you need further help, check out our [video tutorial](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/hyperswitch-open-source/overview/unified-local-setup-using-docker). 👉 After setup, [configure a connector](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/hyperswitch-open-source/account-setup/using-hyperswitch-control-center#add-a-payment-processor) and [test a payment](https://docs.hyperswitch.io/hyperswitch-open-source/account-setup/test-a-payment).

Hosted Sandbox (No Setup Required)

Hyperswitch offers a fully hosted sandbox environment that requires no setup. You can explore the Control Center, configure payment connectors, and test payments directly from the UI.
What you can do in the Hosted Sandbox - Access the full Control Center - Configure payment connectors - View logs, routing rules, and retry strategies - Try payments directly from the UI

Cloud Deployment

You can deploy to AWS, GCP, or Azure using Helm or CDK scripts. Fastest path: Click to deploy via AWS:
Cloud Deployment Instructions 1. Click the AWS deployment button above to launch the stack. 2. Follow the guided steps in the AWS Console (approx. 30–45 mins). ✅ This setup provisions Hyperswitch on your cloud account using CloudFormation. 📘 For full instructions and Helm-based deployments, check out the Cloud Install Guide.

Architectural Overview

 ## Why Hyperswitch? Hyperswitch is a commercial open-source payments stack purpose-built for scale, flexibility, and developer experience. Designed with a modular architecture, Hyperswitch lets you pick only the components you need—whether it’s routing, retries, vaulting, or observability—without vendor lock-in or bloated integrations. Built in Rust for performance and reliability, Hyperswitch supports global payment methods (cards, wallets, BNPL, UPI, Pay by Bank), exposes smart routing and retry logic, and provides a visual workflow builder in the Control Center. Whether you're integrating a full payment suite or augmenting an existing stack with a single module, Hyperswitch meets you where you are. “Linux for Payments” — Hyperswitch is a well-architected reference for teams who want to own their payments stack. We believe in: - Embracing Payment Diversity: Innovation comes from enabling choice—across payment methods, processors, and flows. - Open Source by Default: Transparency drives trust and builds better, reusable software. - Community-Driven Development: Our roadmap is shaped by real-world use cases and contributors. - Systems-Level Engineering: We hold ourselves to a high bar for reliability, security, and performance. - Maximizing Value Creation: For developers, customers, and partners alike. - Community-Driven, Enterprise-Tested: Hyperswitch is built in the open with real-world feedback from developers and contributors, and maintained by Juspay, the team powering payment infrastructure for 400+ leading enterprises worldwide. ## Contributing We welcome contributors from around the world to help build Hyperswitch. Whether you're fixing bugs, improving documentation, or adding new features, your help is appreciated. Please read our [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/juspay/hyperswitch/blob/main/docs/CONTRIBUTING.md) to get started. Join the conversation on [Slack](https://inviter.co/hyperswitch-slack) or explore open issues on [GitHub](https://github.com/juspay/hyperswitch/issues).

Feature requests & Bugs

 For new product features, enhancements, roadmap discussions, or to share queries and ideas, visit our [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/juspay/hyperswitch/discussions) For reporting a bug, please read the issue guidelines and search for [existing and closed issues](https://github.com/juspay/hyperswitch/issues). If your problem or idea is not addressed yet, please [open a new issue](https://github.com/juspay/hyperswitch/issues/new/choose).

part.text:
Here's a summary of the completed fix:

**Root Cause**: In the v2 payments flow, `call_connector_service` and `connector_service_decider` never invoked `complete_preprocessing_steps_if_required` (unlike the v1 flow at line ~4001). Since Airwallex is the only connector requiring pre-authorization preprocessing, v2 card payments with Airwallex would skip the `/api/v1/pa/payment_intents/create` call, leaving `router_data.reference_id` unset and causing the subsequent authorize/confirm request to fail.

**Patch Applied** (`crates/router/src/core/payments.rs`, +61 lines):

1. **`call_connector_service` v2** — Added preprocessing block after `update_router_data_with_payment_method_token_result` (~line 4451). Calls `router_data.preprocessing_steps(state, &connector).await`, extracts the `ConnectorTransactionId` from the response, and assigns it to `router_data.reference_id`.

2. **`connector_service_decider` v2** — Added identical preprocessing block before `create_order_at_connector` (~line 4858) for the Direct execution path, with the same `reference_id` propagation.

Both blocks are gated by `connector.connector_name.is_pre_processing_required_before_authorize()`, which currently returns `true` only for Airwallex, ensuring zero impact on other connectors.
